title: Polypharmacy and Medicines-Related Harm
summary: A clinician-facing guide for recognising medicines-related deterioration in an older person, reconciling treatment, identifying high-risk medicines and arranging safe prescriber-led review.

items.title: Must confirm or exclude
mustConfirmOrExclude: The complete current medicines list, including prescribed, over-the-counter, herbal and recently stopped medicines.
Recent starts, dose changes, formulation changes, missed doses, duplication and administration errors.
A plausible link between medicines and falls, confusion, hypotension, bradycardia, bleeding, constipation, urinary retention, hypoglycaemia, acute kidney injury or sedation.
Renal and hepatic impairment affecting accumulation or dose.
Whether each medicine has a current indication, meaningful benefit and acceptable burden.
Whether the person can obtain, organise, understand and take medicines safely.
items.importantLimitation: Do not abruptly stop essential long-term medicines solely because polypharmacy is present. Changes should be indication-led, risk-assessed and prescriber-owned.

items.title: Confirm from multiple sources
mustConfirmOrExclude: Patient or carer report.
Current repeat list and recent discharge or clinic letters.
Medication administration record, blister pack or actual containers.
Community pharmacy information where available.
Allergies, previous adverse reactions and actual adherence.

items.title: How medicines are actually used
mustConfirmOrExclude: Who orders, collects, stores and administers medicines.
Swallowing difficulty, dexterity, vision, cognition and ability to open packaging.
Use of “when required” medicines and maximum doses.
Duplicate brands, old supplies and medicines borrowed from others.

items.title: Urgent or emergency assessment
urgentFeatures: Suspected overdose, severe sedation, respiratory depression, seizure or reduced consciousness.
Significant bleeding, head injury while anticoagulated, severe hypoglycaemia or serious arrhythmia.
Severe dehydration, acute kidney injury, dangerous electrolyte abnormality or inability to take essential medicines.
No safe person or system available to administer medicines.
implications: Treat immediate threats and contact the appropriate emergency, toxicology or prescriber service.

items.title: Physiology and targeted examination
mustConfirmOrExclude: Full observations, glucose and hydration/perfusion assessment where clinically relevant.
Pulse rhythm, lying and standing blood pressure, neurological state, gait and falls risk when medicines may be contributing.
Evidence of bleeding, infection, fluid overload, urinary retention, constipation, oversedation or other suspected adverse effects.
Relevant blood tests, ECG or medicine-level monitoring when available and indicated.

items.title: Falls, dizziness and hypotension
commonFindings: Antihypertensives, diuretics, nitrates, alpha-blockers, sedatives, opioids, antidepressants or antipsychotics.
Postural symptoms, dehydration, bradycardia or recent dose change.
implications: Measure postural blood pressure when safe, assess hydration and obtain prescriber-led review.

items.title: Confusion, sedation and anticholinergic burden
commonFindings: Opioids, benzodiazepines, Z-drugs, antihistamines, bladder antimuscarinics, antipsychotics or multiple centrally acting medicines.
New drowsiness, agitation, hallucinations, constipation or urinary retention.
implications: Assess for delirium and other causes; reduce avoidable sedative and anticholinergic burden through urgent review.

items.title: Acute kidney injury and electrolyte disturbance
commonFindings: Diuretics, ACE inhibitors, ARBs, NSAIDs or medicines requiring renal dose adjustment during dehydration or acute illness.
Reduced intake, vomiting, diarrhoea, rising creatinine or potassium abnormality.
implications: Assess volume status and renal function, and seek prescriber advice on temporary or permanent changes.

items.title: Bleeding risk
commonFindings: Anticoagulants, antiplatelets, NSAIDs, SSRIs or interacting medicines.
Falls, bruising, melaena, haematuria, anaemia symptoms or head injury.
implications: Use the relevant bleeding or head-injury pathway and confirm indication, dose, timing and renal function.

items.title: Hypoglycaemia
commonFindings: Insulin or sulfonylurea with reduced intake, weight loss, renal impairment or administration error.
Sweating, confusion, collapse, seizure or recurrent low glucose.
implications: Treat immediately, identify the cause and arrange urgent diabetes medication review.

items.title: Indication, benefit and goals
mustConfirmOrExclude: Current indication and evidence of benefit.
Whether the medicine supports the patient’s priorities and expected prognosis.
Preventive treatment timescale versus likely benefit.
Duplicate or conflicting therapy.

items.title: Safety and monitoring
mustConfirmOrExclude: Dose appropriate for age, renal function, hepatic function and weight.
Required blood tests, observations or drug-level monitoring completed.
Interactions, contraindications and cumulative adverse effects.
Clear instructions for acute illness and when to seek review.

items.title: Burden and adherence
mustConfirmOrExclude: Complexity, frequency, formulation, swallowing and packaging.
Cost, access, transport and pharmacy support.
Understanding, capacity and carer administration.
Whether simplification could improve safe use.

items.title: Safe change plan
mustConfirmOrExclude: Named prescriber responsible for each change.
Tapering requirement or withdrawal risk.
Monitoring after the change and expected timeframe.
Communication to patient, carers, GP, pharmacy and other services.

items.title: Record explicitly
mustConfirmOrExclude: Sources used for reconciliation and discrepancies found.
Medicine, dose, route, frequency, indication and actual use.
Suspected adverse effects and supporting clinical findings.
Renal function, relevant monitoring and interaction risks.
Changes made, prescriber authorisation, tapering and monitoring plan.
Who will obtain and administer medicines after the assessment.

items.title: Medicines-related harm
safetyNetting: Any significant deterioration in breathing, chest pain or collapse – call 999.

Seek urgent reassessment for increasing drowsiness or confusion, a further fall, bleeding, black stools, repeated low glucose, inability to take essential medicines, markedly reduced urine output or vomiting that prevents medicines and fluids being retained.
